requirements.requirement: The existing /srv/inventory tree is owned by inventorysvc.
requirements.summary: Final and post-restart observations show the directory, subdirectory, and both existing files owned by inventorysvc:inventory-readers.

requirements.requirement: The existing data is readable by inventory-readers.
requirements.summary: Directories have group traversal/read permissions, files have group-read permissions, and effective group-identity read tests pass before and after restart.

requirements.requirement: Users outside the owner and inventory-readers group cannot access the data.
requirements.summary: ACLs grant no permissions to others throughout the tree, and effective access by an unrelated identity is denied before and after restart.
The same two files remain present, and their SHA-256 hashes match the preparation baseline both after repair and after restart.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct final-state and effective-access evidence. Existing contents were preserved, ownership and reader access were repaired, unrelated-user access was removed, and the result persisted across a fully evidenced node restart.
limitations: Requirement content_preservation cited unknown evidence IDs: prepared-inventory-data

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Creating the missing service account and reader group was a necessary prerequisite; changing ownership, clearing ACLs, and setting modes directly implemented the requested repair. The scheduled reboot served the mandatory restart protocol. No failed services, damaged package state, new exposure, or executor-created residue was observed afterward. Restart evidence is complete: healthy pre-restart state, acknowledgement, bounded connection disruption, changed boot identity, and recovered system, SSH, identities, data, and permissions; fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate it.
